newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shining gains approval for 75 million B shares.
newsitem.headline: Shining gains approval for 75 million B shares.

text.p: Zhuhai Shining Metals Group Inc has received preliminary approval from the Shenzhen Securities Management Office to issue 75 million B shares and list them in Shenzhen, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.
Shining is selecting a domestic main underwriter and an international coordinator for the offer, the official told the Hong Kong-based China Securities Bulletin newsletter.
If the application is approved, Shining would use proceeds from the offer towards construction of an electric power plant in the central Chinese province of Shaanxi, the official said.
Shining has a 51 percent stake in the 380-million-yuan plant, whose construction began in August this year, he said.

The plant is scheduled for 30 percent operation next August and full operation by end-1998. It will have three power generators each with a 50,000 kilowatt capacity and is designed to serve Shining's 51 percent-owned Tongchuan Aluminium Factory in Shaanxi, the official said.
Tongchuan has an annual production capacity of 50,000 tonnes per year of electrolytic aluminium, he said.
With full operation, the power plant should generate 750 million kw/hours of electricity a year and reduce the aluminium factory's annual production cost by more than 20 percent, he said.
Electricity currently accounts for about 40 percent to 50 percent of the factory's annual production cost, he added.
The power plant project will be partially financed by bank borrowings, the official said, without elaborating.
Shining acquired a majority stake in Tongchuan last year, which boosted its earnings and is expected to fuel profit growth again this year, he said.
Shining, based in Zhuhai city in southern Guangdong province, is mainly enagaged in the production, import and export of nonferrous metals.
It has forecast after-tax profits of 56.47 million yuan for 1996, compared with 44.14 million in 1995 and 26.32 million in 1994, under Chinese accounting standards, the official said.
Shining said in an interim report that it had unaudited net profits of 21.99 million yuan in the first half of 1996, compared with 13.49 million yuan in the year-earlier period.
